headline: Agentic AI Foundation adds Agent Skills, Open Responses, OpenEnv and OpenSandbox
lede: The Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation says it now hosts 10 projects, including Agent Skills contributed by Anthropic, and Google's Gary Illyes revised a draft that adds URL-level controls to the Robots Exclusion Protocol.

items.title: Agentic AI Foundation adds four projects, including Agent Skills
items.body: The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) announced four new projects on Oct. 22, 2026: Agent Skills, contributed by Anthropic; Open Responses, contributed by OpenAI; OpenEnv, contributed by Hugging Face; and OpenSandbox, contributed by Alibaba. According to the Linux Foundation, this brings AAIF to 10 hosted projects, up from its three launch projects in December 2025. The new projects join A2A, Agent Router, agentgateway, AGENTS.md, goose and MCP. Our panel check finds Agent Skills published by 46 of 210 panel domains.
items.why_it_matters: Agent Skills, MCP, A2A and AGENTS.md now sit under one foundation. Implementers relying on them should follow AAIF channels for future spec and governance changes.

sources.title: Agentic AI Foundation Announces Four New Projects: Agent Skills, Open Responses, OpenEnv, and OpenSandbox
sources.label: VERIFIED

stats: Agent Skills (anthropic-agent-skills-format) is published by 46 of 210 panel domains.

items.title: Robots Exclusion Protocol extension for URL-level control revised as draft-illyes-repext-04
items.body: Gary Illyes of Google published draft-illyes-repext-04, an Informational Internet-Draft that extends RFC9309 with URL-level controls. The controls can be set through an HTTP response header and through HTML meta tags. The revision moves the header out of the experimental "X-" header space and defines how multiple headers combine.
items.why_it_matters: Sites and crawler operators that use per-URL directives should track the header name change and the new rules for combining multiple headers.

related.name: AI Crawler User-Agent Tokens in robots.txt

items.title: Draft proposes an IANA registry for MCP tool surface names
items.body: draft-morrison-mcp-tool-surface-names-registry-03, an individual Informational draft, asks IANA to create a registry for Model Context Protocol tool surface names. A tool surface name is the wire-level identifier a client uses to invoke a typed capability on an MCP server. The registry would use the Specification Required policy of RFC 8126 with a Designated Expert pool. Its initial contents are four names, one Active and three Provisional.
items.why_it_matters: This is an individual draft with no IETF standing. MCP server authors who want to avoid tool-name collisions can comment on it, but nothing changes in the MCP spec itself.

sources.title: An IANA Registry for Model Context Protocol Tool Surface Names
sources.label: VERIFIED

items.title: New draft defines verifiable mandates for agents acting across domains
items.body: draft-hulea-wimse-agent-mandate-00, an individual draft with Intended status Standards Track, defines how a relying party in one administrative domain validates the mandate under which an agent acts for a principal in another domain. It separates evidence of the delegator's authority from the statement that the mandate was granted. It also specifies a deterministic validation procedure driven by an explicit validation profile.
items.why_it_matters: Relying parties that accept delegated agent actions across organizations can compare this model with other WIMSE and OAuth delegation drafts. It is not a WG document.

items.title: Ad Context Protocol v3.2.6 released
items.body: The Ad Context Protocol project tagged v3.2.6 on GitHub, released 2026-10-23.
items.why_it_matters: AdCP implementers should review the v3.2.6 release notes before upgrading.

items.title: W3C publishes Linked Web Storage Protocol 1.0 Working Draft
items.body: The Linked Web Storage Working Group published Linked Web Storage Protocol 1.0 as a W3C Working Draft dated 23 October 2026, on the Recommendation track. The spec aims to give applications secure, permissioned access to externally stored data in an interoperable way. W3C notes that a Working Draft does not imply endorsement.
items.why_it_matters: This is the core protocol that the LWS authentication suites build on. Teams evaluating LWS-based storage for agents should read it together with those suites.

related.name: LWS 1.0 Authentication Suite: Self-signed Identity using Controlled Identifiers

items.title: Draft revisions: MCP DNS discovery, JAFAR, OAuth agent delegation, delegation receipts
items.body: Datatracker shows several new revisions: draft-morrison-mcp-dns-discovery-09, draft-illyes-webbotauth-jafar-01 (dated 2026-10-22), draft-hamr-oauth-agent-delegation-03 (dated 2026-10-22) and draft-nelson-agent-delegation-receipts-15 (dated 2026-10-22). Separately, draft-ietf-oauth-identity-assertion-authz-grant-04 expires on 2026-11-22.
items.why_it_matters: Implementers tracking these drafts should diff against the prior revisions. Anyone citing the identity assertion grant should watch whether a new revision appears before 2026-11-22.

items.title: More individual drafts on signed receipts for agent actions
items.body: Several individual Informational drafts on recording agent actions were revised. draft-chueayen-attestation-receipts-04 adds an action record, signed with Ed25519 by the enforcement point rather than the agent. draft-zambo-aer1-26 defines execution receipts for tool calls. draft-etcheverry-action-ref-04 derives a deterministic action identifier using RFC 8785 JCS. draft-oga-musubi-settlement-02 recomputes whether recorded acts stayed within a signed grant.
items.why_it_matters: These overlapping proposals have no IETF standing. Teams building audit trails should treat them as input rather than settled formats.

items.title: Panel check: llms.txt at 143 domains, mpp.dev drops to grade B
items.body: Our checks covered 210 of 211 panel domains today. llms.txt is published by 143 of 210 (+1 since 2026-10-23). mpp.dev no longer publishes Agent Skills, api-catalog or Markdown for Agents, and it moved from grade A+ (65) to B (41). Separately, 2058 servers (3000 versions) were published or updated on the official MCP Registry since 2026-10-23.
items.why_it_matters: Site-level signals can disappear between daily checks, so verify current files before relying on a domain's published capabilities.
